evidence.excerpt: Repeated subculturing of Bacillus subtilis ATCC 6633 over 50 transfers was monitored by colony morphology scoring, sporulation frequency counting, and Illumina short-read whole-genome sequencing at transfers 10, 25, and 50. Sporulation frequency declined from 91% at transfer 1 to 67% at transfer 50. Sequencing identified seven single-nucleotide variants accumulating progressively, five mapping within the spo0A regulatory network. Plating-based morphology scoring correlated poorly with variant accumulation until transfer 35, suggesting that phenotypic methods underestimate early genomic instability. Glycerol cryostocks prepared at transfer 5 fully recovered wild-type sporulation and variant profiles after revival, supporting early banking as the primary mitigation strategy. The study provides quantitative thresholds for acceptable transfer number in inoculum propagation protocols used in industrial enzyme production.
